body.x: Raonark (CEO Koo Min-gi) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th (local time).

Raonark is a domestic company that has introduced next-generation smart lock integrated solutions with a differentiated technology to the global market. They focus on a consumer-centric premium smart lock product line and possess various smart lock products, technological capabilities, and service expertise. These include automated door-opening systems and blockchain IoT (Internet of Things) security solutions.

With its technological diversity, Raonark positions itself as a ‘multi-platform’ company in the security field. They strive to develop products optimized for national standards, including fire resistance certification and integration with home networks. Through these efforts, Raonark has gained rich expertise in product planning and technological development, expanding its market presence in various domestic and international markets.

At CES 2024, Raonark showcased its smart lock solution ‘KeyinSV.’ This product goes beyond the typical functionality of digital door locks, actively utilizing audio and video-based sources in the personal authentication process.

At the same time, it maintains the traditional appearance of entry doors, including handles and all hardware components, preserving the original look of the front door. It functions as a wall-mounted module with wireless communication capabilities, offering a variety of features.

The integrated module, a core component of KeyinSV, performs various functions simultaneously, acting as a doorbell, providing facial recognition, transmitting video, and functioning as a black box camera. Equipped with precision sensors, it recognizes the faces of registered household members in advance to unlock the door. It captures images of unknown visitors, sending mobile alerts to users for verification. Additionally, it can display real-time video images captured in the entry door area.

body.cap: The Keyin smart lock series unveiled by Raonark at CES 2024 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In addition, Raonark also introduced the ‘KeyinLX’ solution at the exhibition, which provides optimized convenience specifications for all users, including vulnerable groups such as older people and people with disabilities. This solution features a patented fully automatic keyhole, allowing the door to open without physical handle manipulation.

In particular, it boasts excellent scalability with the ‘Plus Link Platform’ structure, allowing the addition of various authentication modules. According to the company’s explanation, the platform enables convenient use of the smart lock system for individuals with small keys or socially vulnerable groups facing difficulties with the entrance door.

Minghi Koo, the founder of Raonark, expressed his satisfaction, saying, “Through this CES, we were able to communicate face-to-face with buyers with whom we were already in discussions.” He further mentioned, “It was especially pleasing to receive so many positive responses after unveiling products optimized for U.S. specifications planned for release in October this year.”

Furthermore, the founder added, “We had the opportunity to meet with local companies for collaboration on sourcing our modules and sensor product line, which could significantly enhance our influence in the U.S. market.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global innovative technology trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion is being operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. The Seoul Pavilion, which has collaborated with 13 institutions, is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish itself as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Participating institutions include SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
